easy.explain: Surahs 109 to 112. Al-Falaq and An-Nas follow immediately after.
Surahs 105 to 108. Al-Kafirun, surah 109, comes next.

easy.set: The four prophets in the line of Ibrahim through Ishaq
easy.explain: Ishaq was Ibrahim's son, Ya'qub his son, and Yusuf his son in turn. Isma'il was Ibrahim's other son, from whom a different line descends.

easy.set: The three prayers with four rak'ahs
easy.explain: Dhuhr, Asr and Isha each have four obligatory rak'ahs. Fajr has two and Maghrib three.

easy.set: The months in which the two Eids fall, and the two around them
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr falls at the start of Shawwal after Ramadan, and Eid al-Adha on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

easy.set: Four prophets sent to specific named peoples
easy.explain: The Qur'an names the peoples to whom Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb were sent, and describes Yunus and the people of his city.

easy.set: The order of events in a single rak'ah
easy.explain: A rak'ah proceeds from standing recitation, to ruku', to rising, to two prostrations. The tashahhud and salam come at the end of the prayer rather than in every rak'ah.

easy.set: The three stages of the call to Islam in Makkah
easy.explain: The Makkan period moved from private calling, to the public call after about three years, to seeking support in Ta'if and then Yathrib. The decoys belong to the Madinan period.

easy.set: Four well-known companions and what they are best known for
easy.explain: The decoys are scholars of later generations, not companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

easy.set: The three phrases of the tasbih said after the prayer
decoys: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
easy.explain: The well-known tasbih after the obligatory prayer is SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar, commonly counted thirty-three, thirty-three and thirty-four. The decoys are other phrases of remembrance said at other times.

easy.set: The three categories of people the Qur'an opens by describing in Al-Baqarah
easy.explain: The opening passages of Surah Al-Baqarah describe the God-conscious, those who reject, and the hypocrites in turn.

easy.set: Four things forbidden while in ihram
easy.explain: Certain ordinarily permitted acts become prohibited in the state of ihram. The decoys remain entirely permitted.

easy.set: The first four prophets in the traditional list
easy.explain: The conventional ordering of the twenty-five prophets named in the Qur'an begins Adam, Idris, Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim.

easy.set: The last four prophets in the traditional list
easy.explain: The traditional list ends Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa and finally Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets.

easy.set: Three acts that are pillars of Islam but not daily
easy.explain: Zakat is annual, fasting is for one month a year, and Hajj is once in a lifetime for those able. Salah is the daily pillar.

medium.set: The main rites of Hajj on the Day of Sacrifice
medium.explain: On 10 Dhul-Hijjah pilgrims stone the largest pillar, offer the sacrifice, shave or shorten, and perform Tawaf al-Ifadah. Scholars permit some variation in the order.

medium.set: Four surahs of juz 29, in order
medium.explain: Juz 29 begins at Al-Mulk (67). The decoys are surahs 71 to 74, which also fall in that juz but later.

medium.set: The prayers that may be shortened when travelling
medium.explain: Only the four-rak'ah prayers may be shortened to two when travelling. Fajr and Maghrib are not shortened.
The decoys are daughters of the Prophet ﷺ, not his wives — a distinction worth keeping clear.
The decoys all accepted Islam later: Umar and Hamza during the Makkan period, and Khalid and Amr shortly before the conquest of Makkah.

medium.set: Four surahs commonly recited in the Friday prayer and on Fridays
medium.explain: Al-Kahf is commonly recited on Fridays, and Al-Jumu'ah, Al-A'la and Al-Ghashiyah are reported among those recited in the prayer itself.

medium.set: Four of the Ten Promised Paradise (al-Ashara al-Mubashshara)
medium.explain: The ten named in the well-known narration include the four caliphs, Talhah, Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa'id ibn Zayd and Abu Ubaydah.

medium.set: Four more of the Ten Promised Paradise
medium.explain: The decoys are eminent companions who are not among the ten named in that particular narration.

medium.set: The conditions of the prayer before it begins
items: Covering the required areas of the body
The time for the prayer having entered
medium.explain: These are conditions that must be met before the prayer is valid. The decoys are recommended or merely customary, not conditions.

medium.set: Four categories of people exempt from fasting, with the remedy
items: The temporarily ill — make up later
medium.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make the days up later. Those permanently unable give fidyah instead. The decoys have no basis.

medium.set: Four well-known works of Islamic scholarship and their authors
medium.explain: The decoys deliberately mismatch well-known books with the wrong authors.

medium.set: The four Jumu'ah requirements commonly agreed on
items: It falls in the time of Dhuhr
It is preceded by a khutbah
decoys: It must be in the largest mosque
It requires forty attendees in all schools
It must be led by a scholar
medium.explain: Jumu'ah is two rak'ahs in the Dhuhr time, in congregation, preceded by the sermon. Schools differ on the minimum number of attendees, so that is not an agreed requirement.

medium.set: Four voluntary prayers and when they are offered
medium.explain: The decoys are obligatory prayers, not voluntary ones.

medium.set: The four things Surah Al-Asr identifies, in order
items: Except those who believe and do good
And counsel each other to truth and patience
medium.explain: Surah Al-Asr is three ayahs: the oath, the declaration of loss, and the exceptions — faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and patience.

medium.set: Four battles of the Madinan period, in order
medium.explain: The decoys all took place after the Prophet's passing, during the Rashidun caliphates.

hard.set: The twelve Islamic months, the last six
hard.explain: Months seven to twelve. The decoys are from the first half of the year.

hard.set: The Ten Promised Paradise, the last six
hard.explain: The first four of the ten are the Rashidun caliphs. The decoys are eminent companions not named in that narration.
Surahs 25 to 29. An-Nur is 24, immediately before, and Ar-Rum is 30, immediately after.
Surahs 30 to 34. Fatir is 35 and Yasin 36, which follow.

hard.set: The three surahs with exactly three ayahs
hard.explain: Only three surahs have exactly three ayahs: Al-Asr (103), Al-Kawthar (108) and An-Nasr (110). Al-Ikhlas and Quraysh have four, and Al-Fil and Al-Falaq five.

hard.set: The four caliphs and the manner of the end of their rule
decoys: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz — died in office
hard.explain: Three of the four Rashidun caliphs were killed. Hasan ibn Ali, by contrast, ceded authority rather than being removed by force.

hard.set: Six of the Asma al-Husna in their traditional order, positions 6 to 11
hard.explain: The traditional enumeration opens Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, then those listed here. The decoys are the earlier names.

hard.set: Five Makkan surahs among the first twenty
hard.explain: Surahs 6, 7, 10, 11 and 12 are Makkan, while the decoys — surahs 2 to 5 — are Madinan.

hard.set: The six books in the order they are conventionally listed
hard.explain: The conventional listing places the two Sahihs first, then the four Sunan works. Some scholars substitute the Muwatta for Ibn Majah in the sixth position.

hard.set: Four events of 8 AH, in order
hard.explain: Four events fall within 8 AH alone. The decoys belong to 6, 7, 9 and 10 AH respectively.

hard.set: Five prophets named in Surah Al-An'am's list, in the order given
hard.explain: Surah Al-An'am 6:83–86 lists a sequence of prophets. The decoys also appear in that passage, but later in it.

hard.set: The approximate death years of five major mufassirun and historians
hard.explain: The decoys are hadith compilers and jurists of earlier centuries rather than the later exegetes and scholars listed.

hard.set: Five surahs whose names are single Arabic letters or letter combinations
hard.explain: Several surahs take their names from the disconnected letters that open them. Surah Al-Qalam opens with the letter Nun.

hard.set: Five of the surahs revealed earliest, by common accounts
hard.explain: The earliest revelations are generally held to include these. The decoys are Madinan surahs revealed much later. Orderings of revelation differ between scholars.

hard.set: Five surahs placed between 60 and 66 in the mushaf
hard.explain: Surahs 60 to 64. Al-Hashr is 59, At-Talaq 65, At-Tahrim 66 and Al-Mulk 67.
